competitive_position.claim: Threat: Inflation depresses demand as consumers delay purchases or trade down to lower-priced firearms, while short-term supplier commitments leave margins exposed to higher material, component, and labor costs.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: Because competitive differentiation relies heavily on new product launches, costly development delays or poor market acceptance—alongside state laws restricting direct-to-consumer e-commerce sales such as California's January 2026 accessory law—could hurt revenue.

These statutes are being actively enforced, and we are a defendant in one such action.

risks.claim: Tariff policy changes cut prior-year gross margin by 100 basis points, while the latest quarter's 28.7% gross margin relied on $2.9 million of non-recurring tariff refunds (excluding which margin was 26.1%).
quotes: We estimate that higher tariffs negatively impacted gross margin by approximately 100 basis points when compared to the comparable period last year.
The availability, timing, and amount of any tariff refunds remain uncertain and depend on further legal, regulatory, and administrative actions.
These refunds favorably impacted gross margin by approximately 260 basis points and represented a non-recurring benefit.
Excluding the impact of tariff refunds, gross margin for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was 26.1%.

risks.claim: Firearm demand is sensitive to political shifts—including perceived lower federal gun-control risk under unified Republican control—and persistent inflation that causes consumers to delay purchases or trade down.
quotes: For example, we believe demand for our products was negatively impacted in recent years by unified Republican control of the executive and legislative branches of the federal government as a result of a perceived lower risk of federal gun control legislation and regulation.

We believe high levels of inflation have depressed, and may continue to depress, consumer demand for our products as certain firearm consumers have traded down to purchase lower-priced firearms or delayed purchases due to cost concerns.
We expect that inflation will continue to impact us during fiscal 2027.

risks.claim: Operating cash usage of $8.8 million, a $24.4 million inventory build, and capital expenditures projected at $45.0 million to $50.0 million drove cash down to 18,699 (table in thousands) and revolver debt up to $40.0 million.
quotes: Cash used in operating activities was $8.8 million for the three months ended July 31, 2026 compared with cash used in operating activities of $8.1 million for the three months ended July 31, 2025, primarily as a result of a $6.6 million increase in working capital usage, partially offset by higher net income.

We currently expect to spend $45.0 million to $50.0 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027.

As of July 31, 2026, we had $40.0 million of borrowings outstanding on the Revolving Line, bearing interest at a weighted average rate of 5.42%, which is equal to the Adjusted Term SOFR rate plus an applicable margin.
